performance_interpretation: Combined fingerprint operations are 44.7% faster after removing one payload build and installed-build scan; direct call-count tests verify this mechanism.

The four-branch CLI failure workload is 12.6% faster, consistent with removing duplicate fingerprint work in each invocation. Full CLI generation is 1.5% faster and direct generation is effectively unchanged.

Live clock and context-managed gate microbenchmarks are 1.9% and 2.7% slower. These small differences are consistent with the additional direct helper/method calls documented in the item reports. They retain one implementation of the math/admission policy; no speed threshold or output relaxation was applied.

Traced peak memory remains close across generation, protocol and SMB workloads. Gate peak allocations decrease from 2600 to 2432 bytes in both runs; gate retained allocations remain 360 bytes. Runtime state census and targeted retention tests remain the leak acceptance checks, rather than treating one RSS sample as proof.
